desc:
Encoding. The array nxt describes n nodes 0..n-1: from node i you move to node nxt[i], or the path ends if nxt[i] = -1. The structure has no cycles, so every path ends after finitely many nodes.

The path of a node is the node itself followed by all nodes you reach by repeatedly following nxt until the end. Return the first node on the path of a that also lies on the path of b, or -1 if the two paths share no node. (Since both paths follow the same nxt, once they share a node they share everything after it.)

Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra memory by walking two pointers that never need to know the path lengths.

Example: nxt = [2,2,3,4,-1,4], a = 0, b = 1: the paths are 0,2,3,4 and 1,2,3,4, so the answer is 2. If a = 5 and b = 1 the paths are 5,4 and 1,2,3,4 and the answer is 4.
constraints: Following nxt from any node ends after finitely many steps (no cycles)
hints: Putting the whole path of one start into a set and walking the other path against it works. How could you avoid the set?
If both paths had the same length you could walk them in lockstep and compare. The trouble is that the part before the common node can have different lengths.

Let pointer p start at a and pointer q at b; each moves one step per round, and when a pointer falls off the end (-1) it continues from the other start. After at most len(path a) + len(path b) + 1 steps both have walked the same total distance, so they stand on the same node (or both on -1).
editorial: Let the path of a have x nodes before the common part, the path of b have y nodes before it, and the shared part have z nodes (z = 0 if they never meet). Pointer p walks x + z nodes of a's path, jumps to b, and walks y more nodes; pointer q walks y + z nodes of b's path, jumps to a, and walks x more. Both have walked x + y steps before the common part, so they arrive at the first common node in the same round.

If z = 0, both pointers fall off the end after x + y + 2 steps in total and both become -1 at the same moment, so the loop ends with the answer -1 and cannot run forever. The walk takes at most about n + n steps and uses two pointers only. A set based solution is also O(n) time but needs O(n) memory.
